Frequently Asked Questions – Gas Fitting in Camrose

How do I check if an engineer is provincially licensed?

Ask to see their provincial licence card. Check the engineer's name, registration number, and the list of appliance categories they are qualified to work on. You can verify any registration at red-seal.ca or by calling 1-877-682-8772 (TSSA Ontario).

What is a gas safety inspection certificate and when is it required?

A gas safety inspection certificate is the annual provincially licensedty Record that landlords in Canada are legally required to obtain for all rented properties with gas appliances. It must be conducted by a provincially licensed plumber and provided to tenants. Failure to comply is a criminal offence.

Can a plumber do gas work?

Only if they are also provincially licensed. Plumbing and gas qualifications are separate. A plumber without provincial licensing cannot legally touch any gas appliance, flue, or gas pipe.

Key Gas Fitting Terms & Regulations

Essential gas fitting vocabulary and Canadian standards every homeowner in Camrose should know.

Provincial Licensing

Provincial licensing is the Canadian legal requirement for any engineer who works on gas appliances, gas pipes, flues, or meters. Under the provincially licensedty (Installation and Use) Regulations 1998, it is a criminal offence to work on gas without this registration. Every registered engineer carries a photo ID card listing their name, registration number, and the categories of gas work they are competent to carry out. Always ask to see the card and verify it at red-seal.ca before any gas work begins — the register is free to search.

Gas Safety Inspection Certificate

A gas safety inspection certificate is the annual safety record that landlords should obtain for all rented properties with gas appliances for all rented residential properties. It must be carried out by a provincially licensed plumber who inspects all gas appliances, flues, and pipework in the property and issues a signed certificate. Landlords must provide a copy to existing tenants within 28 days of the check and to new tenants before they move in. Failure to obtain a valid gas safety inspection certificate is a criminal offence punishable by fines and imprisonment.

Electrical Safety Certification

Electrical safety certification requirements for plumbing-adjacent work vary by province in Canada. Plumbing and heating work often involves electrical connections — boiler wiring, underfloor heating thermostats, pump controllers — and unless the engineer holds provincial electrical code competency (typically via an NICEIC or ELECSA scheme), a separate certified electrician must sign off the electrical elements. Ask your engineer in advance which elements of the work are within their competency to self-certify.

National Plumbing Code (NPC)

The National Plumbing Code of Canada sets the minimum requirements for sanitary plumbing installations, drainage systems, and water supply systems in new and renovated buildings across Canada. Notifiable work under Part G includes the installation of unvented hot water cylinders (which must be done by a competent person registered with a relevant scheme) and, in new builds, the specification of water-efficient fittings. Always confirm whether your job requires a provincial building code notification to avoid issues when selling the property.

CIPHE

CIPHE — the Chartered Institute of Plumbing and Heating Engineering — is the international professional body for plumbing engineering. Membership indicates that an engineer has met a defined level of technical training, experience, and commitment to continuing professional development. While Red Seal or provincial journeyman certification is not a legal requirement for non-gas plumbing work, it is a strong indicator of professional standards and a useful filter when comparing contractors for complex installations.

CSA Certification

CSA (Canadian Standards Association) certification indicates that a plumbing product, fitting, or material has been tested and certified as compliant with Canadian plumbing and safety standards. CSA-certified products should be used in all new cold and hot water installations in Canada. Using non-certified fittings can void product warranties, fail inspections, and in the case of backflow prevention devices, create contamination risks.
